topic: Process of Establishing an Ex-situ Seed Bank Accession
questionText:
Arrange the procedural steps followed by agricultural scientists to conserve wild plant germplasm in a long-term seed bank:
(I) Collection of mature, viable seeds from diverse wild crop populations across environmental gradients
(II) Thorough cleaning, genetic inspection, and screening to remove pathogens and non-viable seeds
(III) Controlled moisture desiccation to reduce seed moisture content to optimal levels (3–7%)
(IV) Hermetic sealing in moisture-proof foil envelopes and storage in sub-zero freezers (-18 to -20 degrees Celsius)

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Seed banking follows a standardized protocol: collecting wild germplasm, screening/cleaning, precise drying to 3–7% moisture, and sub-zero hermetic storage.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.
